clue.text: Circulatory system forces one to walk to work

definitions.text: Circulatory system forces one to walk to work

parts.words: Circulatory system forces one to walk to work
parts.note: a belt going round and round makes the user walk while staying put; it is also an idiom for a dull, repetitive job

explanation.surface: Sounds like a medical note about blood circulation driving someone to walk to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulatory system' suggests blood and the heart, but here it is a moving belt that loops round. 'Walk to work' means you walk in order to exercise, and the word also hints at the daily grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym machine with a looping belt makes its user walk or run on the spot.

clue.text: The one on the right of them

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Points to whichever person stands on the right of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the right' reads as a position, but it just adds R after THE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun meaning belonging to them, so it stands for 'of them'.

clue.text: Leave scribbled note offering lift

indicators.note: scribbled suggests letters dashed off messily, so the word leave is rearranged

parts.note: TE is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a hastily written note offering a ride or a hand up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scribbled' is the anagram signal, and 'offering' is only a link; 'lift' is the verb meaning raise, not a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it up, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A duck for this celebrated bowler?

definitions.meaning: a male duck is called by this name
Sir Francis ... famously finished his game of bowls on Plymouth Hoe before facing the Armada

explanation.surface: Seems to ask which famous cricket bowler took a duck, a score of nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' and 'duck' both suggest cricket, where a duck is a batsman's zero; the bowler here played bowls, a lawn game rolling balls at a small target.
explanation.definitionFit: A male duck has this name, and Sir Francis the explorer is the legendary player of bowls.

clue.text: Not far out in marine navigation

definitions.text: Not far out in marine navigation

parts.words: Not far out in marine navigation
parts.note: a sailing term for waters close to the coast rather than out at sea

explanation.surface: A sailor's term for staying close in while navigating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not far out' sounds like 'nearly right', but here it means close to land.
explanation.definitionFit: Waters near the coast are described this way, as opposed to offshore.

clue.text: Extensively used sort of folder, found abandoned on table extension?

parts.note: abandoned can mean unrestrained or let go, as in loose living
an extra hinged or inserted board that enlarges a table is called a leaf

explanation.surface: A common type of binder turns up left behind on the added part of a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is a link word here, not part of either piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring binder holding removable sheets is the familiar kind of folder with detachable pages.

clue.text: Belt as part of a shirt

definitions.meaning: to belt someone is to hit them, a slap or blow
the band at the end of a sleeve round the wrist

explanation.surface: A belt worn as a piece of a shirt, which sounds odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' looks like a noun for clothing, matching the shirt, but it is the verb meaning hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a light blow with the hand and the wristband of a sleeve share this word.

clue.text: Local authority, giving sound advice

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for advice is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: counsel means advice

explanation.surface: A town hall that hands out good, sensible guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning sensible, but it signals a soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: The elected body running a town or district is its governing body.

clue.text: Forenames out of place for member of a secret order

indicators.note: letters out of place are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Members of a secret society get their first names wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the fraternal society of Masons, known for secret rituals.

clue.text: King whose wife went to Paris, causing strife

definitions.text: King whose wife went to Paris, causing strife

parts.words: King whose wife went to Paris, causing strife
parts.note: Helen of Sparta left her husband for the Trojan prince Paris, setting off the Trojan War

explanation.surface: Reads like a modern monarch whose wife ran off to the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' looks like the city, but it is the Trojan prince who took Helen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartan ruler in Greek myth, husband of Helen of Troy.

clue.text: Works with potential spouse

indicators.note: potential suggests what the letters could become, so the word spouse is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone works alongside a possible future husband or wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Latin word for a musical or artistic composition.

clue.text: Found note in packing case

indicators.note: in places the note inside the box

parts.note: a crate is a wooden packing case
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A message discovered inside a shipping box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as discovered, but it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a company or school is to establish or bring it into being.

clue.text: Subdued, having arrived after it's finished

indicators.note: after places the word for arrived following the one for finished

parts.note: when something is finished it is over
came is a synonym for arrived

explanation.surface: Someone turned up late, after the event had ended, and was overpowered.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense synonym: to have defeated or conquered.

clue.text: Capital for a ship holding company

indicators.note: holding means the ship's letters wrap around the company

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a set is a group or company of people

explanation.surface: Money set aside for a shipping holding company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding company' looks like a business term, but 'holding' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's capital is its property and resources, valued items owned.

clue.text: Extent of usefulness on board

parts.note: goods last only so long sitting on a shop's board, that is a shelf

explanation.surface: Sounds like how long something stays useful aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, but the board is a shelf in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The period a product stays fit for sale or use while stored.

clue.text: Slightly damaged, so withdrawn

definitions.meaning: marked by a light scrape on the surface
a horse or competitor taken out of a race before it starts

explanation.surface: Something lightly damaged and so taken out of a sale or race.
explanation.definitionFit: A scraped surface, and a runner pulled from an event, share this past participle.

clue.text: A singular spectacle?

parts.note: spectacles come as a pair of lenses; a single one is a monocle

explanation.surface: Seems to describe an unusual sight or show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' looks like 'strange' and 'spectacle' like 'a sight', but it means one lens of a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a lone lens, half of what a pair of glasses would be.

clue.text: Revolutionary comrade at last becomes a politician

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning, so the word comrade is rearranged
last here takes only the final letter of the word at

explanation.surface: A revolutionary comrade eventually turns into a mainstream politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' looks like 'finally', but it gives the last letter of AT; 'Revolutionary' rearranges COMRADE into DEMOCRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Democratic Party is one kind of politician.

clue.text: One who is against work has a problem

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: An objector to a job finds it troublesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who resists or argues the other side is an adversary.

clue.text: Moves near the capital

indicators.note: moves tells us the letters of near the change places

explanation.surface: Someone relocates closer to the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' looks like part of the definition, but it is in the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An older spelling of the name of Iran's capital city.

clue.text: City investment is about to be productive

indicators.note: is about means the investment wraps round the City

parts.note: a fund is a pool of invested money
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: A financial district investment fund is going to bear fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London is the financial district, with postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fertile and fruitful, able to produce abundantly.

clue.text: Company doctor is amusing

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

explanation.surface: A firm's resident doctor turns out to be funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to comedy, therefore funny or entertaining.

clue.text: Cricket side and ground not in harmony

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
a pitch is a playing ground

explanation.surface: A cricket team and its ground are out of tune with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is divided into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing or playing slightly wrong in tone is out of tune.

clue.text: Possibly shoots ducks with graduate doctor

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
a duck is a zero score, so two ducks are O and O

explanation.surface: A hunter fires at ducks alongside a qualified doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoots' looks like a verb about firing at ducks; it is a noun, the edible shoots of this plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoots of this giant grass are eaten in Asian cooking, an example indicated by 'Possibly'.

clue.text: Sailor came up to wrong dock

indicators.note: came up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A sailor arrived at the wrong dock.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed area of water where ships moor is a dock.

clue.text: Man of property, three quarters in gold

indicators.note: in places the quarters inside the gold

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
the quarters are compass points, here west, north and east

explanation.surface: A wealthy man who keeps most of his fortune in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three quarters' looks like 75 per cent, but it means three compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: One who possesses property is its proprietor.

clue.text: Inferior school to get equipment first

indicators.note: first puts the equipment ahead of the school

parts.note: kit is equipment

explanation.surface: A poor school must get its equipment before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacky, tasteless art or design is considered of low quality.

clue.text: Study, entering further exam for junior hospital doctor

indicators.note: entering puts the study inside the further exam

parts.note: a resit is an exam taken again
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: A medical trainee studies for another exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor in hospital training is known by this title.

clue.text: Saline drip?

parts.note: a salty drop falling from the eye when crying

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saline drip' suggests a hospital intravenous line, but it is a salty drop from the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop of salty fluid shed from the eye when weeping.

clue.text: Fast food outlet?

parts.note: a place serving meals on a fast-moving train

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a burger bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food' suggests burgers, but it is food served while travelling fast on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage where passengers eat meals during the journey.
